rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a post-deposition oxidation treatment to form an oxide scale, while the paper uses nanoindentation/friction simulation at different temperatures without any oxidation treatment. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature wear testing near 500°C, while the paper uses nanoindentation simulations at 300, 600, 900, and 1200 K. The temperature regimes overlap partially (500°C ≈ 773 K), but the testing method (wear testing vs. nanoindentation simulation) and specific conditions differ substantially.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a protective oxide scale barrier mechanism, whereas the paper's mechanism involves lattice disorder, dislocation density evolution, and stacking fault to disorder transition. These are entirely different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced wear rate and friction due to an oxide scale, while the paper predicts stable wear resistance up to 600 K then sharp decrease above 900 K with increased friction. The predicted property (wear resistance) is the same, but the direction and underlying cause are different.
